## F08.skill-format — Skill format

Definition: File layout and frontmatter of a skill.
- claude-code [supported, verified] A skill is a SKILL.md file in its own folder, such as .claude/skills/name/SKILL.md; a bare .claude/skills/name.md file does not appear in /skills. A skill directory lets you bundle reference docs, templates or scripts alongside the prompt. Hooks can be defined in skill frontmatter in the same configuration format as settings hooks. | ev: E-claude-code-07620, E-claude-code-06816, E-claude-code-10015
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A skill is typically a SKILL.md file plus optional scripts, references, and assets. Config refers to a skill by the path to a skill folder containing SKILL.md. When present, the server reads interface and dependencies from SKILL.json. | ev: E-codex-cli-03158, E-codex-cli-00559, E-codex-cli-02585
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources. A plugin skill is a skills/NAME subdirectory containing a SKILL.md file; the name and skill description let Copilot determine whether to use it for a task. | ev: E-copilot-cli-02538, E-copilot-cli-01449, E-copilot-cli-01738, E-copilot-cli-02517
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] A skill is a `SKILL.md` Markdown file with YAML frontmatter that defines its metadata and behavior. Definition: Where skills are found, by scope.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Skills are SKILL.md files in .claude/skills/. Skills also come from plugins and .claude/commands/. A customization lockdown can restrict skills from user and project sources so they come only from plugins or managed settings. /reload-skills re-scans skill and command directories so skills added or changed on disk become available without restarting. | ev: E-claude-code-02206, E-claude-code-08026, E-claude-code-00130, E-claude-code-07295
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Skills can be global (in your user directory) or repo-specific (checked into .agents/skills). Skills stored in your repository are available in cloud tasks. ## F08.invocation — Invocation

Definition: Automatic selection versus explicit invocation.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Claude gets a list of available skills so it knows what it can invoke; full skill content loads only when Claude uses one. Skills with disable-model-invocation: true are not in that list and stay out of context until you invoke them with /name. One command's entry notes it also activates automatically when your code imports anthropic or @anthropic-ai/sdk. | ev: E-claude-code-07373, E-claude-code-07230
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Explicit invocation: include the skill directly in your prompt; app-server clients include $‹skill-name› in the text input plus a skill input item. Typing @ invokes a plugin or one of its bundled skills explicitly. The glossary describes skill invocation as explicit or implicit activation of a skill. | ev: E-codex-cli-02794, E-codex-cli-00309, E-codex-cli-01995, E-codex-cli-01724
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] A skill can be invoked via /SKILL-NAME or automatically by the agent; when invoked, its content is injected into the conversation. You can manually invoke a skill with a slash command and list available skills with /skills list. The description frontmatter field (required) says what the skill does and when Copilot should use it. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03628, E-copilot-cli-01740, E-copilot-cli-02459
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] The agent loads a skill when the task matches, or you invoke it directly. Typing `/` in the chat input and selecting the skill invokes it explicitly, and `/‹name›` invokes an agent skill or reusable prompt by name. The `description` field states what the skill does and when to use it, to help Copilot decide when to load the skill. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01943, E-copilot-vscode-02049, E-copilot-vscode-00103, E-copilot-vscode-00541
- cursor [supported, unverified] Automatic: the agent is presented with available skills and decides when they are relevant based on context. Explicit: type / followed by the skill name in chat to run it, or type @ and select it to attach as context. Option+Enter (Mac) or Alt+Enter (Windows) from the / menu starts a skill as a Custom Mode that stays in context on every turn until you exit the mode. | ev: E-cursor-03896, E-cursor-04317, E-cursor-01616
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] The model activates agent skills only when needed. In the code-reviewer example, Gemini identifies that the request matches the skill's description (quote truncated). The activate_skill tool lets Gemini CLI load specialized procedural expertise. The /skills slash command manages Agent Skills. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00045, E-gemini-cli-01442, E-gemini-cli-02113, E-gemini-cli-00593
- grok-build [supported, unverified] Any user-invocable skill can also appear as a slash command, for example `/‹skill-name›`; if names collide, use the qualified form, such as `/local:commit`. `disable-model-invocation` (default `false`) makes a skill slash command only, with no automatic invoke. `user-invocable` defaults `true`; `false` hides it from you and from the model. | ev: E-grok-build-00118, E-grok-build-00039, E-grok-build-00328, E-grok-build-00396

## F08.resource-loading — Resource loading

Definition: How a skill's supporting files load into context.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Skill descriptions load at session start as short summaries; full content loads only when a skill is invoked. An AgentDefinition skills list preloads the named skills into the agent's context at startup; unlisted skills remain invocable through the Skill tool. | ev: E-claude-code-00194, E-claude-code-10581, E-claude-code-00827
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Skills use progressive disclosure to manage context. Skill metadata is loaded and visible to the agent so Codex can choose skills implicitly without bloating context. The available-skills catalog budget defaults to 2% of the model's context window (explicit values capped at 10000 tokens). A skill directory can include a scripts/ folder with CLI scripts Codex invokes in the workflow. | ev: E-codex-cli-02788, E-codex-cli-03157, E-codex-cli-00557, E-codex-cli-03160
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] When a skill is invoked, Copilot discovers all files in its directory and makes them available alongside its instructions; they can include scripts Copilot can run. Org or enterprise remote skills are fetched on demand when invoked. Setting skills to false disables embeddings-based dynamic instruction retrieval for skills. | ev: E-copilot-cli-02461, E-copilot-cli-01739, E-copilot-cli-03638, E-copilot-cli-03751
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Copilot accesses additional files in the skill directory only when the instructions reference them; an unreferenced file is not loaded. A skill can include instructions, scripts, templates, examples, and other resources that the agent loads when relevant. By default, a loaded skill's instructions are added to the parent agent's context window. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01557, E-copilot-vscode-02044, E-copilot-vscode-00113
- cursor [supported, unverified] Skill descriptions are injected into the system context; skills load resources on demand, keeping context usage efficient. A references/ directory holds additional documentation loaded on demand, and a scripts/ directory holds executable code the agent can run, referenced in SKILL.md using relative paths from the skill root. | ev: E-cursor-00065, E-cursor-03895, E-cursor-03941, E-cursor-03940
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Skill metadata (name + description) is always in context (~100 words). The SKILL.md body is loaded only after the skill triggers (‹5k words). Bundled resources are loaded only as needed by the model. When a skill is activated, the model is granted access to this entire directory. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01606, E-gemini-cli-01607, E-gemini-cli-01608, E-gemini-cli-01447
